coverageSpotVerification.detail: I read the source of every mapped test for all 58 suite-required assertions of the seven attempted milestones (M1-M6, M8) — the complete mapping, not a subset — and then re-executed each assertion's observable myself. Every mapping exercises the observable it claims. No mapping was found dishonest, so no milestone is adjudicated to capability-failure. Coverage is also complete: evidence/coverage-manifest.json maps exactly the 58 suite-required assertions of the attempted milestones (M1 7, M2 22, M3 7, M4 5, M5 6, M6 5, M8 6) with no missing entry, and each acceptance run recomputes `missing` from the frozen manifest and fails closed. Three qualifications, none of them dishonesty. (1) m8-a06 and m8-a07's mapped tests assert on booleans stored in evidence/m8-trending-clock.json — an artifact the lane's own scripts/trending-proof.mjs writes on an isolated clock-offset instance — rather than re-deriving the observable at suite time; m8-a05's mapped test additionally needs that isolated backend on port 49363 to be running. The observables genuinely hold: I re-ran trending-proof.mjs from a fresh store and then independently queried insights.trending, re-deriving the >24 h exclusion and building the like-count tie myself. So these three mappings are honest but indirect, and the m8 suite receipt is not self-contained (see defect d-04). (2) Several tests legitimately bundle clauses, e.g. m2-a16's mapped test checks repost attribution at the API level while the UI 'reposted by {display name}' string is proved by the M2 choreography segment and by my own browser run. (3) The test mapped to m2-a06 contains a dead sub-expression (`ids.every((id) => false) ||`) that can never be true; it does not weaken the check that follows, but it obscures what the poll waits for.

defects.summary: A group message's aggregate receipt advances to 'read by all' when an unread member merely leaves the group, instead of staying pinned to the recipient set as of send time. schema.q's receipt() takes the minimum over rows currently in `members`, so deleting an unread member's membership removes them from the requirement rather than holding the aggregate back.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#defect-d-01 — three-member group, Bob acknowledges state 2, Carol never reads: aggregate correctly stays 0; Carol then leaves (removeMember on her own membership) and the aggregate jumps to 2 ('read by all') with no one having read her copy. Source: snapback/schema.q:223-229 (fn receipt) with the members delete rule at schema.q:172.

defects.summary: POST /m/acknowledge returns state:"sent" for a caller who is not a member of the message's chat, while performing no change. The only delivery-acknowledgement operation API.md documents therefore reports success for a call it silently ignored, so a custom client cannot tell 'acknowledged' from 'discarded'.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#defect-d-02 — a freshly registered non-member POSTed /m/acknowledge {ids:["sm0001"],state:2} and received state:"sent"; the message's receipt and all target state were unchanged. Every other non-member write in the same probe was refused terminally (NOT_MEMBER / NOT_ADMIN / MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND / E_RULE). Source: snapback/schema.q:289-302.

defects.summary: The logged notification-provider seam writes to a path it does not create: snapback/worker.mts appends each payload to CLIQUE_PUSH_LOG (default evidence/push.jsonl) without ensuring the directory exists, so on an instance whose log directory is absent every push and digest payload is lost with no visible error while the effect is still acknowledged to the backend.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#defect-d-03 — observed on a grader-created isolated instance whose working directory had no evidence/ folder: the schedule fired and the digest job ran, but no payload was ever recorded. Creating the directory made the same seam record payloads normally. Does not affect the lane's own evidence, where evidence/ exists. Source: snapback/worker.mts (appendFile on `path` with no mkdir).

defects.summary: The documented acceptance entrypoint is not self-contained for M8: `npm run acceptance -- --milestone m8` fails unless scripts/start-proof.mjs and scripts/trending-proof.mjs have already been run, because the tests mapped to m8-a05/a06/a07 read evidence/m8-trending-clock.json and query the separate clock-offset backend on port 49363. The README documents the prerequisite, but it is not expressed in package.json or enforced by the suite, so a clean-checkout m8 receipt can depend on out-of-band state.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#defect-d-04 — I had to start the proof instance and run trending-proof.mjs before the m8 suite would pass on my fresh store; the other six milestones needed nothing beyond backend, seeds and web server. Source: scripts/acceptance-m8.mjs (reads evidence/m8-trending-clock.json; fetches http://127.0.0.1:49363).

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap') and the 90 anchor ('every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts'), and short of 90 on the clause the 90 anchor names explicitly.
O1.justification: 101 of the 119 frozen assertions pass under my own execution: M1 13/13, M2 27/27, M3 15/15, M4 12/12, M5 12/12, M6 6/13, M7 0/9, M8 16/18. Far past the 60 anchor — M5, M6 and M8 are not 'patchy', they are fully green and I reproduced all seven attempted suites (m1-m6, m8) green from a clean checkout against a fresh store, and every web choreography segment is green with a schema-valid, hash-bound receipt. Two structural gaps hold it below 90. First, the 90 anchor requires platform-proof artifacts and none exist: m6-a01..a07 and m8-a17/a18 (9 assertions, all the iOS-simulator cold-start and durable-queue-restart observables) have no recording, no receipts and no run manifest, which the lane declares honestly as pass:null/'not-recorded' rather than inferring from web behaviour. Second, M7's 9 assertions are not-run; applicability.json keeps every in-scope milestone in the denominator regardless of status, so they score not-passed even though the non-attempt was directed by this packet's authoritative scope (attribution, not completeness credit). 78 places the lane about 60% of the way from 60 to 90, matching an 84.9% assertion pass rate with two named whole-category gaps.

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path') and the 90 anchor ('only cosmetic nits'), just short of 90 because one finding is a real correctness divergence rather than a nit.
O2.justification: Beyond the checklist I found one minor defect and three cosmetic ones, and no blocker or major. The one substantive finding (d-01) is a wrong user-visible claim — 'read by all' on a message nobody read — triggered by an unread member leaving the group, diverging from the brief's send-time recipient set; it is narrow, loses no data and has no security effect, and the checklist's own m3-a09 scenario holds. Everything I probed at the trust boundary held server-side rather than by UI absence: unauthenticated reads of every query refused 401; a registered non-member reading another pair's DM gets empty arrays and nulls for thread/apiHistory/roster/room/searchChat/whoTypes/message; private DM assets serve only the member (member 200, registered non-member 404, anonymous 401); a third party cannot burn a view-once view; sender/author arguments are rejected outright (E_INPUT) so the bearer alone determines the caller; non-member writes are refused NOT_MEMBER/NOT_ADMIN/MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND/E_RULE with target state unchanged; refusal codes give no existence oracle (promote on a real invisible chat and on a nonexistent chat both return NOT_ADMIN); replaying a write id stores exactly one message; receipts are monotonic and out-of-range states refused BAD_RECEIPT; input bounds hold at the documented 1..2000 edge; tombstones preserve the id, empty the body and remove it from in-chat and global search; and paging stayed exact through 25 identical timestamps. 86 rather than 90 for d-01; well above 60 because there are no medium defects at all.

O4.anchorsCited: Above the 60 anchor's failure description ('reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush' — none of which happened) but below 60 overall, because the 90 anchor's requirement ('all behave as specced on the native proof - on full runs including M8's durable-queue restart and multi-device convergence evidence') is unmet for the whole cold-start and durable-restart half of the dimension. Well clear of the 30 anchor ('cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app'), which describes an observed failure that did not occur.
O4.justification: Scored only from the harness's mechanically checkable artifacts, never from builder assertions. What the artifacts do demonstrate, on schema-valid receipts: warm-offline search over previously synced messages with no restart (m5 warm-offline-search, 1057.1 ms); two messages composed offline in the web client showing pending state, flushing on reconnect in exact order and reaching read (m6 offline-message-queue-flush-in-order, 4123.4 ms); and M8's multi-device evidence, where two warm-offline Alice clients each queued a message and converged in observed server-arrival order with no loss and no duplicates, receipts then advancing normally to read (m8-a15/a16). What is absent is the dimension's named primary basis: there is no iOS-simulator artifact at all, so cold-start offline history, cold-start media, cold-start search, the view-once-never-durably-cached guarantee, and the durable-queue-across-app-restart proof (9 assertions) are wholly unevidenced — no m6/m8-ios-screen.mp4, -receipts.jsonl or -run.json exists anywhere in the lane. Honesty of the gap is exemplary and is what keeps the score from falling toward 30: the segment summaries carry supplementalExternal pass:null status:'not-recorded', the README states plainly that no simulator proof is claimed, and setup-identity.json declares no qualified binary or wrapper — nothing is inferred from web behaviour or relabelled as a native pass. 55 credits genuinely demonstrated ordered offline writes, correct post-flush receipts and warm-offline reads, and debits roughly half the dimension's observables having no artifact.

O5.bandRationale: First-match over the frozen order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75.
